answer: Delay-function occupancy resists sybils. Each key locks a slashable bond and must extend a unique delay chain on a fixed cadence. Heads must land before a public horizon; a missed beat, reused intermediate, or two chains from one prover slashes every linked deposit. Occupancy is logged under a raven serial that cannot be reassigned mid-epoch. Each key files a short sonnet of recent heads and bond ids so peers can audit uniqueness. One core cannot keep many delay chains at pace, so a farm needs distinct live compute and bonds for every identity; attacker cost scales with hardware and capital.
